justification: One familiar move (odd-function property) applied once, with a mild disguise in the inverse-hyperbolic form. Same level as the simple king-property integral 2026-P2-Q4 (L1).

key_step: Divide by $n$ to read $f(j/n)$, convert to $\int_0^1\frac{2x+8}{2x+4}dx$, split into $1+\frac{2}{x+2}$.
justification: Three routine stages (Riemann sum to integral, division of the fraction, log evaluation) with no new idea and options to check against, like the routine chain of 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).

key_step: Reflection $x\to-x$ kills $e^{x\cos x}$; then $\int_0^{\pi/4}\frac{dx}{\sin^4x+\cos^4x}$ via $t=\tan x$ and $t-\frac1t$.
justification: Two well-practised tricks chained (king property with $e^{g}$, then the standard $\sin^4+\cos^4$ integral), no unusual idea, options available. Comparable to the king-property chain of 2024-P2-Q16 (L2).

Single familiar theorem (Rolle) applied twice with FTC to translate, plus the distinctness check; short and option-based. Below the multi-statement Rolle/IVT question 2021-P2-Q3 (L4); level of a routine chained question like 2023-P2-Q1 (L2).

key_step: Nested-log domain reduces to $18x-x^2-77>3$, i.e. $(8,10)$; then $a+b-x$ pairing gives $\frac{b-a}2$.
justification: Two stages, each routine: domain of nested logs (careful but standard) then the king property on $\frac{f}{f+f(a+b-x)}$. No options, but short. One step above the bare king-property question 2026-P2-Q4 (L1) because of the domain stage.

key_step: Do not differentiate blindly: use $\int_3^x F'=F(x)-F(3)=F(x)$ to solve for $F(4)$, and differentiate $e^xF$ for $F'(4)$.
justification: Integral equation with $F$ and $F'$ inside, so the usual differentiate-and-solve-DE route is not enough; one must see that the $4F'$ part integrates exactly. Same family as 2023-P2-Q1 (L2, integral equation to linear DE) with a twist and a numerical answer, so one level higher.

key_step: Symmetry about $\pi/2$, substitution $\cos^2x=t$, and by parts on $t^{-1/2}e^t$ to produce $\int\sqrt t\,e^t$.
justification: Four stages (symmetry, substitution, split, by parts) with the target form given only implicitly, numerical answer. Heavier than the L2 king-property integral 2024-P2-Q16 but each move is standard, so it stays at 3 rather than the L4 of 2025-P2-Q16.

key_step: Factor $(x-1)^8$ out of the root so the integrand is $(x-1)^{-2}\left(\frac{x+2}{x-1}\right)^{-5/4}$; then $t=\frac{x+2}{x-1}$.
justification: Two routine moves (rewrite under the root, ratio substitution) with options to differentiate-check; a well-known JEE Main pattern. Similar routine chain to 2026-P2-Q3 (L2, separable DE with finish).

key_step: Shift to $x+\frac12=\frac{\sqrt3}2\tan\theta$, reduce to $\cos^2\theta$, convert $\sin2\theta$ back.
justification: Standard trig substitution chain of five or six routine steps with algebraic back-conversion; no insight but numerical with no options, so slip-prone. Routine-chain level like 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).

key_step: Write numerator as $A\cdot D+B\cdot D'$ and integrate to $Ax+B\ln D$.
justification: One familiar trick (numerator = A*denominator + B*derivative) applied once, followed by two linear equations. Same level of a single standard move as 2026-P2-Q4 (L1).
